title: Reminiscences of an Independent Director
keywords: Hernandez Napocor Forbes Park wires cancer
primary_topics: Talk to the Good Governance Advocates and Practitioners of the Philippines (GGAPP), October 16, 2019 -- recounting CJP's career as an independent director (ID), non-executive director (NED) and adviser across a dozen publicly-listed companies over 12 years

The Meralco corporate coup attempt (2008): CJP's crucial on-the-spot legal advice to the Lopez Group that the SEC restraining order was void ab initio, enabling Chairman Manolo Lopez to proceed with the election and retain control

The definition of an ID's main duty: fidelity to the corporation -- not to the majority, not to the minority, not to any shareholder, but to the law that authorized IDs and to the ideals of good corporate governance

CJP's four personal criteria for accepting directorships: comfortable with major shareholders and company culture; no contentious rivalry conflicts; substantive preparation and transparency; strict time management and self-discipline
sub_topics: Age-and-forgetfulness joke opener: the Jolly Restaurant group of men -- at 40 (pretty waitresses), 50 (good food and wine), 60 (sunset view), 70 (wheelchair accessible, elevator), 80 (they had never been there before)
CJP's entry into Meralco: called from New York City (tending to newborn grandson Matthew) by Chairman Manuel M. Lopez; immediately flew back for the May 27, 2008 shareholders meeting

The SEC coup attempt: a shareholder read an ex-parte SEC order restraining proxies favoring the Lopez Group; CJP opined it was 'invalid and gravely abusive'; the Lopez Group held 37% + 17% restrained proxies (54% total) vs. GSIS/SSS/Land Bank coalition at 42%; if the order were followed, minority would control the company; CJP advised Chairman Manolo could not simply adjourn (government reps could hold election by default); Manolo ignored the SEC order and proceeded; manual count till midnight; 5 Lopez + 4 GSIS coalition + 2 IDs (Panlilio and CJP); SEC Restraining Order later declared void by the judiciary

Contentious Meralco board meetings: minority leader repeatedly harangued the Chairman; shooed away executives (including a retired SC justice as general counsel who resigned feeling insulted); CJP acted as referee; minority leader invited CJP to his private pre-meeting caucuses; CJP was able to 'quiet him down and he became more reasonable and less virulent'

Hernandez v. Napocor (March 23, 2006): SC ordered Napocor to cut/relocate high voltage wires atop Tamarind Road (Forbes Park/Dasmarinas Village boundary); no conclusive evidence of cancer causation but Court played it safe; decommissioning would cause massive Metro Manila blackout plus severe Meralco financial losses; CJP convened complainants, lawyers, and Chairman Lopez at his home; after seeking WHO and other expert opinions, no conclusive medical finding supported the cancer suspicion; complainants desisted from seeking execution

GSIS/SSS/LandBank exit: sold Meralco shares to San Miguel Corporation; four SMC directors replaced government reps; Lopezes then asked CJP to advise between two suitors (Ramon Ang of SMC or Manny Pangilinan of MPIC); CJP recommended Pangilinan because he already knew him as MPIC director and had observed him 'run MPIC fairly and competently'

Petron entry: on Ramon Ang's last day as Meralco director, he offered CJP a Petron ID ('walang conflict diyan, kasi wala namang petroleum business si Manny'); CJP sought and got Pangilinan's permission first ('I fully trust you and I know you will not reveal our secrets')

PLDT NYSE investigation: a group of US investors alleged that PLDT top officials (including chairman and president) defrauded the company via overpriced intermediary companies; instead of just denying, the PLDT Board asked CJP to conduct an 'independent, objective and thorough investigation'; CJP rendered a voluminous report exonerating all officers; offered to testify at US SEC if needed; 'I was staking my career and reputation as a retired Chief Justice on the accuracy, objectivity and truth of my report'; investors never filed a complaint

Jollibee NED: Tony Tan Caktiong (CJP's PLDT board seatmate as NTT Docomo representative) invited CJP as Independent Adviser then ID; SEC rejected ID nomination (had served as adviser); Tan Caktiong nominated him as NED representing his shareholdings -- 'my rejection as an ID was a blessing in disguise' (no term limits; can represent majority shareholder interests)

MPIC entry: offered by Chairman Manny Pangilinan, introduced by Marixi Prieto; 'at that time, MPIC invested in only one business -- as the controlling shareholder of Maynilad Water Services'; CJP witnessed its growth into Meralco, tollroads (Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand), 14 hospitals (Makati Med, Asian Hospital), LRT 1, logistics

ID's main duty: 'The main duty of every director... is fidelity to the corporation... to promote and uphold the interests of the corporation above and beyond the pecuniary wants or desires of any shareholder... What makes an ID different is precisely his or her independence from them, and to uphold truth, fairness, transparency, accountability and good corporate governance'

Four personal criteria: (1) comfortable with major shareholders and company culture; (2) no contentious rivalry conflicts (with permission of both if rivals are friendly); (3) substantive preparation (studies financials, speaks with CFOs, watches for related-party transactions and ethical issues); (4) strict time management and self-discipline

stances.claim: An Independent Director's primary duty is fidelity to the corporation -- not to the majority, not to the minority, not to any shareholder or group of shareholders. IDs owe loyalty only to the law that authorized their creation and to the ideals of good corporate governance. This is CJP's definitive answer to the common misconception that IDs represent the minority.
stances.rhetorical_move: fidelity-to-the-corporation principle as the definitive refutation of the 'IDs represent the minority' misconception
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing principle of CJP's corporate governance philosophy

stances.claim: The 2008 SEC Restraining Order against the Lopez Group's proxies at the Meralco shareholders meeting was void ab initio -- an ex-parte order that, if obeyed, would have constituted irreparable harm to the Lopezes and Meralco by allowing a 42% minority coalition to control the company. CJP's on-the-spot legal advice to ignore the order, proceed with the election, and let the judiciary resolve the validity question was the decisive intervention that preserved proper corporate governance.
stances.rhetorical_move: void-ab-initio legal analysis as the decisive intervention preserving corporate governance
stances.confidence: asserted as a real-time legal opinion that was subsequently vindicated by the courts

stances.claim: Retirement from the judiciary merely meant 'a change of tires to embark on a new independent journey in the business world.' CJP's 12+ years as a corporate director have exceeded the duration of his 11-year SC tenure -- demonstrating that post-judicial relevance is not an accident but the product of discipline, substantive preparation, and principled governance.
stances.rhetorical_move: change-of-tires self-application: corporate directorship as the continuation of an independent career, not a retirement from it
stances.confidence: asserted through the quantitative comparison (12+ years corporate vs. 11+ years SC)

notable_anecdotes: The Jolly Restaurant age joke: a group of men at 40 (pretty waitresses), 50 (good food and wine), 60 (beautiful sunset from veranda), 70 (wheelchair accessible, has elevator), 80 (they had never been there before) -- a perfectly constructed comedic arc about aging forgetfulness, delivered as CJP's self-deprecating opener for an audience he warned not to re-invite an octogenarian speaker.

The Meralco corporate coup (2008): CJP was in New York tending to newborn grandson Matthew when he received Chairman Manolo Lopez's call. At the shareholders meeting, after the SEC Restraining Order was read, Oscar Lopez asked CJP's private opinion -- the order appeared 'invalid and gravely abusive'; if followed, the minority (42%) would control the majority; if Manolo adjourned, government reps could hold the election by default. CJP advised proceeding. The election lasted till midnight, the longest in corporate memory. The SEC order was later declared void by the judiciary.

Hernandez v. Napocor resolution: CJP convened complainants (his Dasmarinas Village neighbors), lawyers, and Meralco's Chairman Lopez at his home -- pointing out that a decommissioning of the wires would 'raise havoc in Metro Manila compared with the yet inconclusive suspicion' of cancer risk. After WHO and international expert opinions found no conclusive causal link, the complainants desisted from seeking execution of the SC's own final and executory decision.

The Petron entry dialogue: Ramon Ang on his last Meralco day: 'Chief, I thought you only knew law. Having observed you, I now know you also know business pala.' Offered SMC directorship; CJP declined (conflict with MPIC); Ang: 'Please join Petron -- walang conflict diyan, kasi wala namang petroleum business si Manny.' CJP sought and got Pangilinan's permission: 'Tama naman si Ramon, we have no conflict with Petron. Besides, I fully trust you and I know you will not reveal our secrets.'

The PLDT investigation: US investors alleged the PLDT chairman and president defrauded the company via overpriced intermediaries. CJP conducted an independent investigation, rendered a voluminous report with video recordings, transcripts and documentary evidence, exonerating all officers. 'I was staking my career and reputation as a retired Chief Justice on the accuracy, objectivity and truth of my report.' The investors never filed with the US SEC.

Jollibee NED: Tony Tan Caktiong (CJP's PLDT seatmate as NTT Docomo representative) offered CJP an ID nomination; SEC rejected it because CJP had served as an adviser. Tan Caktiong nominated him as NED representing his shareholdings. CJP: 'my rejection as an ID was a blessing in disguise' -- no term limits, can represent majority shareholder interests.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered October 16, 2019 to the Good Governance Advocates and Practitioners of the Philippines (GGAPP) at SM Aura, this speech by CJP -- opened with the Jolly Restaurant aging-forgetfulness joke (group of men who at 80 agree to meet there because they had never been there before) -- recounts 12+ years of corporate directorship experience. The centerpiece is the 2008 Meralco corporate coup: called from New York by Chairman Manolo Lopez while tending to newborn grandson Matthew, CJP flew back in time for the May 27, 2008 shareholders meeting where an ex-parte SEC restraining order was read to block the Lopez Group's proxies. Advising patriarch Oscar Lopez privately that the order was 'invalid and gravely abusive' and that obeying it would allow a 42% minority coalition to control the company, CJP recommended proceeding with the election -- the manual ballot count ran till midnight, the longest in corporate memory, and the SEC order was later judicially voided. He also narrates his Hernandez v. Napocor intervention (convening Dasmarinas Village complainants at his home to find a win-win solution that resulted in their desisting from executing the SC's own final order once WHO and international experts found no conclusive cancer-radiation link), the Petron entry (Ramon Ang's last-day offer after observing CJP: 'I thought you only knew law -- I now know you also know business pala'; permission sought from and given by Pangilinan: 'I fully trust you and I know you will not reveal our secrets'), the PLDT NYSE investigation (CJP's independent voluminous report exonerating top officials, staking his career and reputation on it; investors never filed), and the Jollibee NED (SEC rejected him as ID; Tony Tan Caktiong nominated him as NED instead -- 'my rejection as an ID was a blessing in disguise'). He articulates the ID's main duty -- fidelity to the corporation, not loyalty to any shareholder -- and his four criteria: culture fit, no contentious rivalry, substantive preparation, and strict time management. He closes: 'retirement merely meant a change of tires to embark on a new independent journey in the business world.'
